etymologies.etymologyHTML: Shortened from taximeter cab, taximeter (“automatic meter that records distance and fare”) from French taximètre, from German Taxameter (whence also English taxameter), coined from Medieval Latin taxa (“tax, charge”). More at tax, task.

definitions.definition: A vehicle that may be hired for single journeys by members of the public, driven by a taxi driver.

quote.citation: 1932, Delos W. Lovelace, King Kong, published 1965, page 12:
quote.text: "Taxi," he called. And when one pulled up to the curb with screeching brakes he ordered, "The nearest restaurant."

quote.citation: 2007 August 24, Graham Linehan, The IT Crowd, Season 2, Episode 1:
quote.text: [Sobbing uncontrollably] I thought I could make it work between us because you looked a bit like a man.TAXI!

definitions.definition: (aviation) The movement of an aircraft across an airport's surface under its own power; a phase of aircraft operation involving this movement.
To move an aircraft on the ground under its own power.

quote.citation: 1932, Delos W. Lovelace, King Kong, published 1965, page 1:
quote.text: [H]e had taxied to the waterfront bent upon a business in which nostalgia had no part[.]
